After breakfast, transfer to the airport for the flight to the Galápagos Islands. At Baltra Airport, your guide will meet you and help with your luggage.

The drive to the Itabaca Channel takes about 10 minutes. From there, a motorboat takes you across to Santa Cruz in around 5 minutes. Puerto Ayora is approximately a 45-minute drive from the channel. Along the way, the island’s dry, reddish northern terrain gradually gives way to green highlands.

In the farming areas of Santa Cruz, you may see local birds, including the famous finches associated with Darwin’s research. The main focus of the tour is the giant tortoises. On private farms, they roam freely in their usual habitat. You may see young tortoises with smooth shells and older individuals whose shells show the marks of a long life. Your guide explains how local farms help protect the tortoises and their habitat.

Next, visit the lava tunnels. They formed as lava flows cooled: the outer layers hardened while molten lava continued moving inside. Some sections have collapsed over time, but you can still walk through passages with hardened lava formations and fallen boulders.

Lunch is included. After the tour, transfer to Puerto Ayora, check in and enjoy the evening at leisure.

**Accommodation:** Solymar, 4-star, Ocean View Room.  
**Meals:** Breakfast and lunch.
A yellowish-brown iguana on dark coastal rocks, Galápagos, Ecuador
Galápagos Islands: an iguana against blue water and breaking surf

Early in the morning, head to the Itabaca Channel and board a yacht. The crossing to Bartolomé takes about 2 hours. Watch the ocean along the way. In favourable conditions, dolphins and other marine animals may appear alongside the boat.

After landing, walk uphill for about 30 minutes through volcanic terrain. From the top, you can see Santiago, North Seymour, Baltra, Santa Cruz, Rábida and the islet of Chinese Hat. Nearby stands Pinnacle Rock, one of the Galápagos’ most recognisable natural landmarks.

After the walk, the tour continues along the coast. From the boat, you may see Galápagos penguins, which stand about 50 cm tall. Look for them by the rocks or swimming quickly through the clear water.

There’s time at the beach for swimming and snorkelling. In the water, you may see reef sharks, starfish, rays, sea turtles and colourful tropical fish. On shore, look for marine iguanas, sea lions and pelicans.

Lunch is served on board. Return to Puerto Ayora by evening, with time at leisure.

**Accommodation:** Solymar, 4-star, Ocean View Room.  
**Meals:** Breakfast and lunch.
